offence_severity: Life imprisonment for the offence under Section 302 IPC and rigorous imprisonment for ten years for the offence under Section 376 read with 511 IPC
physical_harm: Death caused by asphyxia as a result of throttling
premeditation_planning: The court found that the accused had made an attempt to commit rape
key_evidence_accepted: Medical report clearly says that the death was caused due to asphyxia as a result of throttling. PW-4, the surgeon, who conducted the autopsy, stated that the deceased was wearing a shirt. In the FIR, it was clearly mentioned that the accused strangulated the deceased with the help of her shirt. The medical report supports the same.
witness_credibility: The High Court has treated Ganeshi as a natural and neutral witness and it has also observed that his evidence could not have been thrown overboard on the ground of absence of precise description of distance and the fact that he had not seen the children bathing in the water. The High Court has found that the reasoning ascribed by the trial court to disbelieve the version of PW-2 is unacceptable.
post_offence_conduct: The accused was apprehended at the spot.
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the accused attempted to commit rape on a 9-year-old girl and caused her death by strangulation. The medical report confirmed the cause of death was asphyxia due to throttling, and the witnesses' accounts supported the accused's actions.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the trial court correctly identified discrepancies in the witnesses' testimonies and that the prosecution failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt. They also claimed the High Court's reversal of the acquittal was based on minor discrepancies.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that an appellate court has the power to review all evidence and reverse an acquittal if the trial court's findings are perverse or unreasonable.
precedent_relied_upon: Jadunath Singh v. State of UP, AIR 1972 SC 116; Oamodar Prasad Chandrika Prasad v. State of Maharashtra, AIR 1972 SC 622; State of Bombay v. Rusy Mistry, AIR 1960 SC 391; and other cases cited in the judgment.
sentencing_rationale: The sentence of life imprisonment and 10 years rigorous imprisonment was imposed due to the heinous nature of the crime, the attempt to commit rape on a minor, and the consequential death of the child, which has a devastating effect on society.
judicial_aggravating_factors: The crime was an attempt to commit rape on a 9-year-old girl, which destroyed the social equilibrium and had a devastating effect on the family and society.
